correctness.rationale: Write baseline S=1−F, h0=f/S. The transformed hazard is hS=h0 Phi(S), Phi(s)=(π s/2)cot(π s/4)=2y cot y. Its derivative in y is 2(sin y cos y−y)/sin²y<0 for 0<y<=π/4, so Phi(S(x)) increases strictly with x and h0 positive nondecreasing makes hS strictly increasing. For New X–Lindley S0=e^(−ξz)(1+ξz/2), h0=ξ(1+ξz)/(2+ξz), increasing. Limits Phi(1)=π/2, Phi(0+)=2 imply πξ/4<hξ(z)<2ξ. As t=ξz→∞, Phi(S0)=2−π²S0²/24+O(S0⁴), and h0/ξ=1−1/(t+2), yielding z(2ξ−hξ(z))→2. This is analytic for all z>0, ξ>0; numerical grid checks cannot replace it.
